content.text: To show an argument is **invalid**, find a counterexample: truth values that make every premise true and the conclusion false.
Start by making the conclusion false. Then try to make each premise true.

examples.title: Affirming the consequent
lines: The argument: P → Q, Q, so P.
Try P false and Q true.
P → Q is true and Q is true, but P is false.

examples.title: Denying the antecedent
lines: Try P false and Q true.
P → Q is true and ¬P is true, but ¬Q is false.

question.prompt: How do you show that an argument is invalid?
options: Show that a premise is false
Find a case with true premises and a false conclusion
question.hint: Validity says that something can never happen. Show that it can.
question.explanation: A counterexample makes every premise true and the conclusion false. One is enough to show invalidity.
